questions.stem: Which is NOT a classic clinical manifestation of parvovirus B19 infection?

options.label: C
options.text: Transient aplastic crisis in a patient with chronic hemolytic anemia
options.html: Transient aplastic crisis in a patient with chronic hemolytic anemia

options.label: D
options.text: Severe fetal anemia with nonimmune hydrops
options.html: Severe fetal anemia with nonimmune hydrops

questions.solutionHtml:
Correct answer: B — Polymyalgia rheumatica

Classic B19 manifestations include fifth disease, adult arthropathy, suppression of erythropoiesis causing aplastic crisis in chronic hemolytic disease, persistent anemia in immunocompromised patients, and fetal anemia with hydrops. Polymyalgia rheumatica is not a classic manifestation. This distinction does not assert that every reported rare association is impossible. Fetal anemia results principally from impaired red-cell production, not direct hemolysis.

Which of the following upper limb muscles is bipennate?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Dorsal interossei

 

Let's discuss each of the given options :

 

Option A. Palmar interossei: The palmar interossei are intrinsic muscles of the hand located between the metacarpal bones. Their primary function is adduction of the fingers, i.e., bringing the fingers toward the midline (toward the third finger). These muscles are unipennate, meaning their muscle fibers run obliquely from one side to a central tendon.

 

Option B. 1st lumbrical: The lumbricals are four muscles in the hand that have the primary function of flexing the metacarpophalangeal joints and extending the interphalangeal joints. The 1st lumbrical originates from the radial side of the tendon of the flexor digitorum profundus of the index finger. This muscle is not bipennate; instead, it has a simpler structure extending from its origin to its insertion.

 

Option C. 2nd lumbrical: The 2nd lumbrical, like the other lumbricals, assists in flexing the metacarpophalangeal joint and extending the interphalangeal joints. It originates from the radial side of one tendon and the ulnar side of the adjacent tendon of the flexor digitorum profundus. However, despite this dual origin, the muscle itself is not structured in a bipennate manner.

 

Option D. Dorsal interossei: The dorsal interossei are four muscles located between the metacarpal bones in the hand. Their primary function is to abduct the fingers, meaning they move the fingers away from the midline (away from the third finger). Structurally, these muscles are bipennate, having fibers that run from both sides to a central tendon, giving them a feather-like appearance.

A 5- year-old boy is brought to the office by his parents after exposure to a child with a rash. Three days ago, the patient had a day-long playdate with a friend who had low-grade fever and a vesicular rash. That child and another child in the neighbourhood were subsequently diagnosed with chickenpox. The patient has no symptoms and no history of medical problems. The boy received age-appropriate vaccinations in infancy but has not received any immunizations after age 1. The boy's mother is currently pregnant and immune to the varicella zoster virus. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination of the skin, ears, and mucous membranes is normal; the remainder of the examination is unremarkable. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in the management of this patient?

options.label: D
options.text: Administer varicella vaccine and varicella immunoglobulin

questions.stem: A 25-year-old man comes to the office due to right hand pain and swelling. He injured the skin over his right knuckles when he punched a man in the teeth during a bar fight 3 days ago. The patient ignored the wound initially, but his hand became more painful and swollen yesterday. The patient received a tetanus toxoid vaccination at age 18. Temperature is 37.3 C (99.1 F), blood pressure is 120/70 mm Hg, and pulse is 78/min. There are small lacerations over the right third and fourth metacarpophalangeal joints with surrounding erythema swelling and tenderness. No discharge or crepitus is present. Hand radiographs reveal no foreign body. Which of the following empiric antibiotics is most appropriate for this patient?

An 18-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department with severe vomiting, diarrhoea, and dizziness that started this morning. Three days ago, she had nasal bleeding that required anterior packing in the emergency department. Yesterday, she had pain and a sensation of pressure under her left eye and scant blood-tinged nasal discharge. The pain was relieved by acetaminophen and ibuprofen. The patient has a history of asthma and allergic rhinitis. Her last menstrual period was 3 weeks ago. She does not use tobacco, alcohol, or ilicit drugs. Her temperature is 38.9° C (102.2° F), blood pressure is 90/60 mm Hg supine and 66/45 mm Hg standing, pulse is 120/min and respirations are 23/min. She appears alert but restless. On examination, there are diffuse, confluent erythematous macules on her trunk and extremities. The oropharynx appears hyperaemic. Laboratory results are as follows: Platelets-55,000/uL Leukocytes-9,500 cells/uL Bands-30% Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following structures is present in the male urethra but is not present in the female urethra?
